claims.text: The FeCoNiCrAl feedstock has a particle-size range of 15–45 μm.
The 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock was previously used successfully with the HVAF-M3 torch.
Increasing the HVAF-i7 nozzle-to-substrate distance to approximately 300–350 mm will increase particle velocity.
Increasing particle velocity will improve deposition efficiency.
Greater deposition efficiency will overcome the HVAF-i7 coating-thickness limitation.
A 300–350 mm spray distance will retain coating integrity and minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
Higher particle velocity increases the impact energy of molten particles.
Higher impact energy improves particle flattening, interparticle or substrate bonding, and packing efficiency.
Improved flattening, bonding, and packing efficiency produce a thicker and more adherent coating.
A longer particle flight path allows particles to accelerate to higher velocities.
The increased spray distance reduces particle residence time in an oxygen-rich spray environment.
Reduced residence time in an oxygen-rich spray environment limits excessive in-flight oxidation.
Thermally sprayed HEA powder is susceptible to in-flight oxidation under high-temperature, oxygen-rich conditions.
Default HVAF-i7 settings produce inadequate FeCoNiCrAl coating thickness despite acceptable coating quality.
HVAF-M3 deposition of the same 15–45 μm feedstock produces acceptable coating quality and thickness.
The increased-distance HVAF-i7 process will produce a thicker coating than default HVAF-i7 deposition while maintaining integrity and low oxidation.
The intervention will remain effective for coating internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
The resulting coating will remain suitable under elevated-temperature thermal-barrier service conditions.
Conventional MCrAlY studies indicate a modest deposition-efficiency gain at the proposed nozzle distances.
The optimal HVAF-i7 distance and quantitative thickness improvement have not yet been determined.

contradictions.description: The intervention creates a longer flight path, but the mechanism simultaneously claims that this produces reduced particle residence time. No compensating velocity-time calculation or other explanation reconciles a longer path with shorter residence time.

A 300–350 mm nozzle-to-substrate distance is prescribed while deposition is also required within a 120 mm internal diameter. Without a specialized angled, axial, or remote-nozzle geometry, these spatial requirements are incompatible.
